description: A block of source code — a bordered, tinted surface with mono type, an optional filename/copy header, an optional line-number gutter, and Prism syntax highlighting themed from tokens. Sized xs–xl; `data-density` scales the padding. Compound subcomponents (CodeBlock.Tabs/Header/List/Trigger/Content/Copy) add a tabbed variant that composes the headless Tabs primitive and reuses the tabs component's classes.

props.name: code
props.description: The source to render.

props.name: filename
props.description: Filename shown in the header; its presence shows the header + copy control.

props.name: language
props.description: Prism language id (e.g. `tsx`, `css`, `bash`). Defaults to `tsx`.

props.name: showHeader
props.description: Force the header (with the copy control) even without a filename.

props.name: showLineNumbers
props.description: Show a line-number gutter. Ignored under `variant="inline"`.

contractProps.name: variant
contractProps.description: Presentation. `block` is the standalone code surface; `inline` is a chip that sits in a line of prose or beside a label — same highlighting, same syntax palette, no header or gutter.

contractProps.name: size
contractProps.description: Type size; `data-density` scales the padding further.

contractProps.name: wrap
contractProps.description: Whether long lines reflow to the container. Wrapping is the default because a horizontal scrollbar reads worse on a narrow viewport. Turn it off for content whose column alignment IS the content — a tree with aligned trailing `//` annotations, a table of values — where reflowing a line drops its annotation onto the next row and makes it read as belonging to the row below. The block then scrolls inside its own box.

props.name: activationMode
props.description: When a focused trigger becomes active; see {@link TabsActivationMode}.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Value of the tab active on first render.

props.name: dir
props.description:
Reading direction; see {@link TabsReadingDirection}. Inherited from the
nearest `DirectionProvider` when omitted, falling back to `"ltr"`.

props.name: lazyMount
props.description:
When `true`, a panel's children are not rendered until that tab is first
activated. Once mounted they remain in the DOM across subsequent tab
switches (lazy mount, not unmount-on-hide). Useful for panels that own
expensive initialisation — e.g. a scroll-snap carousel whose initial
scroll position must be set while the panel is visible.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired on every user-driven activation with the activated tab's metadata.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the requested value when the user activates a tab.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout axis; see {@link TabsOrientation}.

props.name: size
props.description: Type size for the block; `data-density` scales the padding.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of the currently active tab.

props.name: wrap
props.description:
Whether long lines reflow to the panel. Turn it off for content whose column
alignment is the content; the panel then scrolls horizontally.

props.name: ariaLabelledBy
props.description:
Id of an existing element to use as the tablist's accessible name,
set as `aria-labelledby`. Mutually exclusive with `label`.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name for the tablist, announced as `aria-label`. Pick a
short, human-readable description of the set (e.g. `"Account
sections"`, not `"Tabs"`). Mutually exclusive with `ariaLabelledBy`.

props.name: value
props.description:
Identifies this trigger, linking it to the `Tabs.Content` of the same
value. Not the visible label — use `children` for that.

props.name: asChild
props.description:
Render the child element instead of the default `<button>`. All tab
ARIA attributes and event handlers are merged onto the child. The child
must accept a `ref`. Useful for routing links that need tab semantics.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Removes the trigger from the roving tab order and marks it
`aria-disabled`/`data-disabled`; arrow-key navigation skips it.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Ref to the rendered element. Defaults to `HTMLButtonElement`; when using
`asChild`, specify the child's element type (e.g. `HTMLAnchorElement`).

props.name: code
props.description: The source for this panel.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of the trigger this panel belongs to.

props.name: language
props.description: Prism language id (e.g. `tsx`, `css`, `bash`). Defaults to `tsx`.

props.name: showLineNumbers
props.description: Show a line-number gutter.

props.name: asChild
props.description:
Renders the child element instead of a native `<button>`, merging all
props — aria-*, data-*, event handlers, ref — onto it via
{@link Slot }. `type` is not forwarded in this mode; the child owns its
own type semantics. See the `asChild` example on {@link Button }.

props.name: children
props.description:
Button content. Defaults to the copy/check icon (swapping on success); pass
text (e.g. `Copy`) for the text form.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
Forwarded to the underlying `HTMLButtonElement`, or — under
`asChild` — merged onto the rendered child via {@link Slot }.

props.name: type
props.description:
The button's native `type` attribute, restricted to the three valid
values. Defaults to `"button"` (not the DOM's own default of
`"submit"`), so a `Button` placed inside a `<form>` never triggers an
accidental submit unless set explicitly.
